competition.text: Daily/weekly/monthly cleaning schedules and planner bundles are common on Etsy and free on blogs. Generic supply is high; we found no products using the exact three-bucket wording.

gap.text: A short (5-per-bucket) version using the trend's exact wording, with pet, plant and car add-ons and vertical slides for people who want to post their own version.

lens: First-spark hunt: food, home, pets and household micro-trend
name: Once a Day, Once a Week, Once a Month Routine Format

origin.text: Named in SocialBee's 29 September 2026 TikTok roundup and described in INFLOW Network's September 2026 roundup. We did not identify the originating video.

spread.text: Two independent marketing-trend roundups list it in September 2026. We have no view counts and no direct TikTok access.

summary: A September 2026 TikTok format where creators split a routine (skincare, fitness, cleaning, business) into three buckets: once a day, once a week, once a month.

what: A short-video or carousel format: the creator shows their routine in three labeled buckets. Roundups say it covers skincare, fitness, cleaning, content creation and business routines. It is a format rather than a method, so it can be applied to home care, pets and plants.

invalidators: The format disappears from roundups in October

window.reasoning: Format trends typically fade fast, but the underlying product category (cleaning schedules) is evergreen, so the main risk is low visibility, not expiry.
